description: A bundle: a reified super-node that names a SET of member records ("these belong together"). Unlike a relation it is NOT an n-ary predicate over its members — there is no subject/object and no claim about how the members relate; it is a flat, unordered membership set. Members may be ANY record with a CID — discourse nodes (question/claim/evidence/study/source/protocol), relations (e.g. supports, addresses, grounds, derivedFrom, versionOf), or OTHER bundles (recursive composition). A bundle is a SET, never an arguer: bundles are not legal endpoints of supports/opposes (those are strictly evidence→claim), so a 'paper A rebuts paper B' headline exists only as its granular edges — never as a bundle-level assertion. It reuses the same DNA as RRGI relations: it is independently authored, carries provenance, and each member is dual-addressed via com.atproto.repo.strongRef (uri + cid, CID mandatory) so the set pins exact content versions and cannot rot. A bundle is just the set; a narrative (tech.scios.rrgi.narrative) is a bundle WITH prose, and a paper is a narrative sitting over a bundle. Evolution is by versioning: edit a bundle by publishing a new bundle record + a tech.scios.rrgi.versionOf edge to the prior one (records are immutable, content-addressed by CID), so 'living' and 'frozen snapshot' are the same mechanism — every version is a citable CID. RRGI-authored (no coalition equivalent). Intended to be proposed upstream.

name.description: Human-readable label for the bundle (e.g. 'Core-Satellite Model — supporting graph').

items.description: Dual-addressed reference (URI + CID) to one member record. com.atproto.repo.strongRef requires both uri and cid, so the CID is mandatory and the membership names the exact content version. A member may be any record: a discourse node, a relation, or another bundle (recursive).

members.description: The set of member records that belong to this bundle. Flat and unordered (any reading order is carried by a narrative's prose, not the bundle). At least one member required.

description.description: Optional description of what this bundle IS — the rationale for grouping these members. This is metadata about the set, NOT the narrative prose (the written argument lives on a tech.scios.rrgi.narrative record).
